bullets.title: The Most Important Question of Your Life
bullets.creator: Mark Manson
bullets.note:
. I could reread this once a week and still benefit. Excellent reminders all around.  
​  
​**“**[**So you wanna de-bog yourself**](https://www.experimental-history.com/p/so-you-wanna-de-bog-yourself)**”** by [Adam Mastroianni](https://substack.com/@experimentalhistory). I only found Adam in July of 2024, but his writing is some of the most hilarious—and helpful—I’ve seen in a long time. Really worth the read. Deep bow to Crazy B for sending this to me.  
​  
​**“**[**A message for the New Year**](https://www.instagram.com/p/C1m0vOnLSD0/?hl=en)**”** from [Brandon Stanton](https://tim.blog/2018/06/18/brandon-stanton-humans-of-new-york/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit), creator of [Humans of New York](https://www.humansofnewyork.com/). This relates to something he and I have texted about often: attention. How should you think about protecting your own attention in 2026? If you don’t have attention, the time and money you have matter very little. Attention is the mother resource. Brandon’s post was first written in early 2024, but it’s more essential with every passing day. This is one life raft for a post-AI world.  
​  
​**“**[**101 Additional Advices**](https://kk.org/thetechnium/101-additional-advices/)**”** by [Kevin Kelly](https://kk.org/). Regular readers know that I consider Kevin one candidate for [the real-world most interesting man in the world](https://tim.blog/2023/04/26/kevin-kelly-excellent-advice-for-living/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content).  
​  
​**“**[**Masters of Love**](https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2014/06/happily-ever-after/372573/)**”** (_The Atlantic_). [Alternate link if you have trouble with the former](https://archive.is/2024.03.12-072741/https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2014/06/happily-ever-after/372573/). This is the best article on courtship, love, and dating that I’ve read in years. It’s not only well-researched and full of memorable insights, it’s very actionable and gives labels to concepts you can use. Ignore the terrible subheadline, which makes it seem like an obvious throw-away piece. The article is _much_ more interesting and helpful than the subheadline implies.  
​**​  
“**[**Why You Should Seek More Awe in the New Year**](https://tim.blog/2024/01/24/awe/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content)**”** by [Ashley Stimpson](https://www.ashleystimpson.com/). Every time I’ve done a [past-year review (PYR)](https://tim.blog/2025/12/26/past-year-review/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit), a pattern emerges: peak positive emotional experiences are correlated to awe at least 70% of the time. For at least the past 3–5 years, this has been so consistent that I often determine what big blocks to schedule in the new year based on potential for awe. The payoffs include [time dilation](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C2cdhDQO7_S/?igsh=MTk4M3lhc2diZjVjNA%3D%3D) and, more broadly, traversing the miraculous canvas of full human experience. Friends have asked me why I do silent retreats in nature, why I love ski touring, why I hunt once in a blue moon, or why I am deeply interested in psychedelic science and [psychedelic-assisted therapies](https://saiseifoundation.org/). If I had to sum it all up in one word, it would be: Awe. But what exactly is “awe,” and how can we embrace more of it? I haven’t found a better article exploring these topics than Ashley Stimpson’s “[Awestruck](https://hub.jhu.edu/magazine/2023/winter/science-of-awe-psychedelics/),” featured in [Johns Hopkins Magazine](https://hub.jhu.edu/magazine/2023/winter/science-of-awe-psychedelics/), so I asked for permission to publish on my blog, which was graciously granted. I hope you find it as thought-provoking and helpful as I did.  
​  
​**“**[**63 Principles**](https://nabeelqu.co/principles)**”** by [Nabeel S. Qureshi](https://x.com/nabeelqu). Nabeel is currently a stealth startup founder but was previously at Palantir. He has been a visiting scholar in AI at the Mercatus Center as well as an Emergent Ventures awardee.  
​  
​**​**[**Coach Christopher Sommer’s email to me**](https://tim.blog/2026/01/02/the-single-decision/)**.** [Coach Sommer](https://www.instagram.com/christophersommer1/?hl=en) is a former U.S. National Team gymnastics coach and the creator of [GymnasticBodies](https://www.gymnasticbodies.com/). This personal email sent to me, which I reread often, was so good that I had to include it in [_Tools of Titans_](https://www.amazon.com/Tools-Titans-Billionaires-World-Class-Performers/dp/1328683788/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20). Make the one big decision.  
​  
​**“​**[**You don’t need more time**](https://seths.blog/2011/02/you-dont-need-more-time/)**”** by [Seth Godin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yhc1sM2NnQY). And [his follow-up expansion](https://seths.blog/2018/07/the-timedecision-gap/).
